findings.title: templateActions guard now blocks when templateSetKey empty
findings.why_it_matters: The old guard was `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey) { ... if (!linked) return false; }`. When template_actions entries existed but state.templateSetKey was empty/null, the old code fell through and returned true (authorable). The new guard is `if (templateActions.length) { if (!tsk) return false; ... }`. Now when template_actions exist and templateSetKey is empty, it immediately returns false (blocked). This is a runtime behavior change: any prefix that has template_actions entries will be blocked for all actions whenever templateSetKey is not yet set (e.g., on page load before a template is selected, or when state.templateSetKey is cleared). Previously those actions would have passed through as authorable. If this was intended as a bug fix it should be documented; if it was meant to be a pure extraction it is a behavioral regression.
findings.suggested_fix: If the intent is pure extraction (no behavior change), restore the old combined guard: `if (templateActions.length && tsk) { const linked = ...; if (!linked) return false; }`. If the new stricter behavior is intentional, document the semantic change explicitly in the PR and update the canonical spec.
evidence: OLD (workbench.js removed): `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey) {` — only enters the block when BOTH conditions are true; empty templateSetKey skips the block entirely, returning true.
NEW (workbench-template-gating.js line 55-56): `if (templateActions.length) { if (!tsk) return false;` — enters the block when templateActions is non-empty, then immediately blocks when tsk is empty.
Test at workbench-template-gating.test.js line 306-313 confirms the NEW behavior (expects false); the OLD code would have returned true for that same input.

findings.title: templateScope empty-array semantics changed from pass to block
findings.why_it_matters: OLD guard: `if (templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily)) return false;` — when skin_family_scope is an empty array, templateScope is an empty Set, templateScope.size is 0, so the condition is falsy and execution continues (action passes through). NEW guard: `if (templateScope !== null && (!templateScope.size || !templateScope.has(skinFamily))) return false;` — when skin_family_scope is an empty array, templateScope is a non-null empty Set, !templateScope.size is true, so it returns false (blocked). An empty skin_family_scope array previously meant 'no scope restriction' but now means 'block everything'. Any ts objects in production data that carry an empty skin_family_scope array will have all their actions blocked after this change.
findings.suggested_fix: Determine which semantic is correct for an empty skin_family_scope array. If empty means 'no restriction' (old behavior), restore: `if (templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily)) return false;`. If empty means 'block all' (new behavior), document the intent and verify no production template-set objects have empty skin_family_scope arrays that relied on the old pass-through.
evidence: OLD (workbench.js removed): `if (templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily)) return false;` — short-circuits on empty Set because `templateScope.size` (0) is falsy.

NEW (workbench-template-gating.js line 42): `if (templateScope !== null && (!templateScope.size || !templateScope.has(skinFamily))) return false;` — !templateScope.size is true for empty Set, causing early return false.
Test at workbench-template-gating.test.js line 203-208: `ts.skin_family_scope = []` expects toBeFalse() — confirming the new behavior; old code would have returned true for this input.

findings.title: Unchecked destructure of window.__workbenchTemplateGating crashes IIFE
findings.why_it_matters: The destructuring `const { BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER, ... } = window.__workbenchTemplateGating;` executes unconditionally at IIFE startup. If window.__workbenchTemplateGating is undefined (script load failure, CSP block, or script tag removed/reordered), this throws `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER' of undefined`, which crashes the entire IIFE and makes the workbench completely inoperative with no meaningful error message. The HTML ordering is correct today, but the absence of any guard means any load failure is a silent catastrophic failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a guard before destructuring: `if (!window.__workbenchTemplateGating) { throw new Error('workbench-template-gating.js must be loaded before workbench.js'); }` — this preserves the failure but with a clear diagnostic message instead of a cryptic TypeError pointing at the destructure line.
evidence: web/workbench.js line 6996-6997: `const { BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER, isTemplateActionAuthorable: _isTemplateActionAuthorable, getEnabledActions: _getEnabledActions } = window.__workbenchTemplateGating;` — no null/undefined check before destructuring.
web/workbench.html line 538-539: correct load order exists, but no runtime guard in workbench.js itself.

workbench-template-gating.js lines 93-99: only assigns window.__workbenchTemplateGating when `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, which is always true in a browser — but the assignment only happens if the script executes successfully to completion.

residual_risks: The two behavior changes (empty templateSetKey with template_actions, and empty skin_family_scope array) may be intentional tightening of the gating logic rather than bugs. If production registry data never has empty skin_family_scope arrays or exercises the empty-templateSetKey path with template_actions populated, the runtime impact is zero. However this cannot be determined from the diff alone.

The test suite tests the NEW behavior for both changed cases, not the OLD behavior. If the old behavior was correct, the tests are validating the wrong thing and will not catch a future reversion to correct behavior.

No integration test covers the workbench.js wrapper functions (isTemplateActionAuthorable/getEnabledActions as closures over state). The unit tests bypass state entirely, so a regression in how state.templateRegistry or state.templateSetKey is forwarded would not be caught.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the transition: template_actions populated + templateSetKey changes from empty to non-empty at runtime (the critical state transition where old vs new behavior diverges).
No test for the old behavior of empty skin_family_scope (old: pass-through; new: block) — making it impossible to tell from the test suite whether the semantic change was intentional.

No test for the workbench.js wrapper layer — specifically that state.templateRegistry and state.templateSetKey are correctly forwarded. A mock-state integration test would catch forwarding regressions.
No test for the load-order failure path: what happens when window.__workbenchTemplateGating is undefined at workbench.js startup.
